## Declared assumptions and kT's decisions

- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-10-26.** Torch heat package (kT, 2026-10-25): each pellet is wrapped in a shell of remass that soaks up the burn and leaves as exhaust. The shell must let no more than ~358 ppm of the burn's energy escape as light, counting its own glow (the reactor face's 10 MW/m2 limit); the design value is 180 ppm. With the model's other assumptions (torch/torch_heat_inputs.json: light 40% of fusion energy; He3-rich, spin-polarised fuel with 0.76% neutrons, 85% absorbed by the shell; plume contact 1e-4 of charged energy; coil shield transmission 1e-3), 1.40 GW reaches hot structure and 0.48 MW the magnet coils at 12.6 TW of fusion. These are assumptions, not results. Replaces v0.5.1's 387 MW (34 ppm) torch-leak gap. Decision: v0.5.2 torch heat package (kT chose the package and 1,750 K fins on 2026-10-25 and accepted this wording the same day): the remass shell lets no more than ~360 ppm of the burn's energy escape as light, counting its own glow; design value 180 ppm; with the heat model's other assumptions 1.40 GW reaches hot structure and 0.48 MW the magnet coils.
- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-10-26.** Hot fins run for life at 1750 K. Lithium heat pipes have run in lab tests to ~1,500 K and briefly ~1,800 K; years at 1750 K with burn cycling and neutron exposure is an engineering extrapolation (a technology milestone), not new physics. Fallback: 1,500 K fins, ~49 m span, ~30 t, still inside the reserve. Decision: kT: "Let's go 1750." Hot fins at 1,750 K, recorded as an engineering extrapolation (technology milestone), with 1,500 K fins as the fallback.
- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-10-26.** Plant electrical: Metric HARD at a 1300 K reject temperature needs 34.8 MW of cryo-chain electrical power, against canon's 23.9 MW at 900 K. The relational plant must supply this (canon amendment), or the cryo chain must reject through a 900 K loop. Decision: canon states the relational plant supplies ~34.8 MW for Metric HARD at a 1,300 K reject temperature. Option not taken: a 900 K loop for the cryo chain.
- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-10-26.** Berth viewports (v0.5.7): 10 x 0.5 m viewports keep the berth screen because acrylic plugs carry at least the g/cm2 they replace (armour 27.14 vs 27.0, ring 8.26 vs 8.0), so the ray screen, which treats the hull as continuous, is unchanged. Rev 3: the same plug kit is in every opening below the crown, including the L2 viewport band, and continues through the storm-shelter jacket (17 cm more acrylic for the 20 cm of water). Not yet shown: the dose. Acrylic is ~8% hydrogen by mass against water's 11%, so per g/cm2 it may stop cosmic-ray secondaries slightly less well; a transport check may ask for a thicker plug. Encapsulated for fire. Decision: Every opening below the crown carries an acrylic shield plug and insert with at least the g/cm2 they replace (armour 27, berth ring 8, shelter jacket 20), so berths and shelter keep their screens with the shutters open; the dose is accepted as a provision until a transport check (OLTARIS) is run; plugs are encapsulated and counted as fire load.
- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-10-26.** Crown dome (v0.5.7): 25 m2 of glazing inside r 2.8 m replaces the 8 nose windows. Assumes (1) proof-tested transparent ceramic panes up to 2.3 m across (2026's largest are ~0.76 m), a 2226 materials milestone like the 1,750 K fins (rev 4: the L2 viewport band's 16-18 mm plate panes rely on the same ceramic; 2026 ALON would need 25-29 mm); (2) tambour gores of armour-equivalent Strata laminate (Builder-derived, MHL-22) that restore 27 g/cm2 when closed and stow in the brow ring; (3) the operating rule: open only at low speed or with the bow facing away from the dust flow (braking and tail-first coasting); closed for solar particle events, radiation belts, torch burns and Loom formation and translation. Stuck closed is safe; stuck open: turn the bow out of the dust flow. With the gores open, L1 loses the armour over the crown (glass 2-9 g/cm2); L1 is not a shelter. Decision: Crown dome over L1 and the L2 viewport band: proof-tested transparent ceramic panes up to 2.3 m (band panes 16-18 mm plates) as a 2226 materials milestone; tambour gores and shutters of armour-equivalent Strata laminate (Builder-derived, MHL-22); the dome and shutters open only at low speed or with the bow out of the dust flow, closed for solar particle events, radiation belts and torch burns.
- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-10-26.** Storm shelter life support: 72 h for 10 people from the life-support room on the same deck (design provision, not computed). Decision: 72 h of life support for 10 people in the storm shelter, from the life-support room on the same deck, recorded as a design provision to be sized in detail later.
- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-10-26.** Galactic cosmic rays: at 2026 free-space rates (1.8 mSv/day, ~657 mSv/yr) a crew member reaches NASA's 600 mSv career limit after ~333 days in deep space. Hull shielding barely changes this. Long careers aboard rely on canon's off-Earth MED-MOD-RADIATION milestone and crew time-in-space rules; this is a canon question, not something the hull can close. Decision: crew protection from galactic cosmic rays relies on canon's off-Earth MED-MOD-RADIATION milestone plus crew time-in-space limits.
- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-10-26.** Torch neutrons and gammas: the shadow shield must attenuate the torch's neutron and gamma output so the dose rate inside the habitat during burns stays within crew limits. The v0.5.2 heat model puts neutrons at ~0.76% of the burn's energy with 85% absorbed by the remass shell; the dose itself is not computed here, only the shadow geometry is checked. Decision: covered by the same declared gap: the torch and shadow shield keep neutron and gamma dose in the habitat within crew limits during burns; the shadow geometry is checked (G6).
- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-10-26.** Torch thrust-vector control: the magnetic nozzle steers the thrust line by up to 1.0 deg (asymmetric coil current). Needed: trim plus an assumed 0.5 deg thrust error (0.846 deg). The error is an engineering assumption, not a measured disturbance history; the authority is not a qualified nozzle capability. Decision: Declare 1 deg of torch thrust-vector authority (decision 2), on the assumed 0.5 deg thrust error.
- **AWAITING.** Axial RCS: one 25 kN thruster per cluster, canted 10 deg outward (bow ones exhaust forward, aft ones aft). Assumes the plumes clear the crown glazing, hull, hot fins and torch chain; plume impingement is not yet modelled.
- **AWAITING.** Long torch burns split into segments of at most 165 min ([V2 6113]) with 15 min coasts (engineering assumption; in free space the coasts change elapsed time, not delta-v).

Script verdict on certification: NOT YET: at least one gate is OPEN or FAIL, or a declared assumption awaits kT. Sign-off still needs both reviewers and loom-gate.

- Net habitable volume by deck: L1 51 m3, L2 81 m3, L3 77 m3, L4 57 m3, L5 57 m3
- Windows: the crown dome over L1 (25 m2), a panoramic viewport band round L2 (19.4 m2, 1.6 m tall in the lounge), 12 round viewports (4 shoulder on L1; L4 medical 2, storm shelter 2; L5 suits 1, workshop 2, vestibule 1) and 10 berth viewports (0.5 m) on L3. With every shutter open about 2.03 kW radiates through the low-e glazing; shutters close for night. The canon candidate suggests 10-16 windows; amendment v2.4f proposes more (kT's call). Below the crown every window has four panes, a dust shutter, a 12 deg armour splay and an acrylic shield plug
- Casualties move at 0 g (coast on the captain's order); under thrust they are treated in their couch or berth.
- Decks are perpendicular to the thrust axis; under thrust, aft is down. Above ~1.5 g everyone rides in a couch.
- Cabins by occupancy (v0.5.3, Sol's candidate): Captain's cabin 1 (15.6 m3 each), Crew cabin A 2 (7.8 m3 each), Guest cabin 4 (5.9 m3 each), Crew cabin B 3 (7.8 m3 each); 10 berths in 4 cabins. Private cabins removed by kT on 2026-10-25 (basis change, Sol to agree).
